## Findings
- claim-1: **Definition 2.1.** “Call an integer tuple \(\varphi=(n,r,i,j,a,b,N)\) valid if \(n,r,i,j,a,b,N\ge1\)” and \[ r<n,\quad a+j\le r,\quad a+i\le n-r,\quad b\le i,j,\quad N\le ab. \] [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 300-304]
- claim-2: **Lemma 2.5.** For valid \(\varphi\), a homogeneous degree-\(N\) syzygy \[ \sum_{\substack{\lambda\subseteq b^a\\|\lambda|=N}}\bar s_{(i^j,\lambda)}f_\lambda =\sum_{\substack{\lambda\subseteq b^a\\|\lambda|<N}}f_\lambda\bar s_{(i^j,\lambda)} \] with nonzero left side implies consistency of the decomposable equations, whose right side is \(f_{\nu_B}\) for tall \(\nu\) and \(0\) for wide \(\nu\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 326-341]
- claim-3: The proof of Lemma 2.5 adds no restriction beyond its stated valid-tuple and syzygy hypotheses: it obtains consistency by deleting equations from the larger system. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 342-344]
## Strategy
Use ledger claims 1–3: Definition 2.1 is at lines 300–304; Lemma 2.5 and its proof are at lines 326–344. Separate valid-tuple conditions from the lemma’s syzygy hypotheses. The requested target is established.

## Gaps
None. No later proof restriction, including \(N\le\min(j,n-r-i)\), is imported.
